name: Spring Security @PreAuthorize disabled with permitAll/true
attack_scenario: Any unauthenticated or low-privilege user calls the state-changing endpoint (e.g. delete/admin action); the always-true expression grants access.
negative_test_hint: send an unauthenticated DELETE request to "/users/1" and assert the endpoint answers 401 or 403 rather than performing the deletion

exemplar.explanation: @PreAuthorize("permitAll") / "true" / "isAnonymous()" evaluates to always-allow, so a method that looks protected is open to everyone. Developers often add it thinking it restricts access. Sensitive methods need a real authority/role expression. isAuthenticated(), hasAuthority(...), and SpEL principal checks do not match.
